messages:
maya: Heads-up — hitting drift on quantized bring-up for a 13B variant. After ~8k tokens the output diverges and we see KV index misalignment warnings. Repro is on dedicated-dev.
maya: Quick symptoms: repeated prompts with small random prepends, after a few rotations the model repeats or inserts garbage tokens. FP16 run is stable.
tomas: Can you paste the exact warning? stack/log snippet?
maya: Log excerpt below:
```text
[WARN] kv_cache_align: expected_row_start=196608, actual_row_start=196609, token_offset=1
[ERROR] attention: kv_index overflow (wrapped) -> falling back to slow-path
```
maya: Happens only on INT8 quant channel. Model: r2-13b, rope_base=10000, kv_packing=packed_kv_quant.
sara: who owns the quant packing kernel? @dylan?
ci-bot: build/452 failed — unit test kv-index-alignment on quantized kernels. https://ci.redwood/builds/452

dylan: I can take this. Maya, can you paste the minimal reproducer and the model cfg you used (quant params)?
maya: Repro gist:
```python
# minimal repro
from redwood import Model
m = Model("r2-13b", quantize="int8", kv_packing=True)
prefix = "user: hello\n"
long_block = "lorem ipsum " * 1200
for i in range(15):
  prompt = prefix if i%2==0 else "user: hi\n" + prefix
  out = m.generate(prompt + long_block, max_new_tokens=64)
```

maya: Quant args: qgroup=64, scale_mode="per_block", reorder=true

dylan: Running local smoke now. Hypothesis: the quant packing kernel computes stride in bytes and later code assumes stride in tokens -> off-by-1 when block compression changes row size.

ana: (typo) I mean ana: I saw a similar issue in a different codepath — quant reorder can change row alignment when using 8-bit pack with odd seq-len.

ana: also: check rotary index wrap handling if kv indices are recomputed after packing.

tomas: Also verify attention mask cumulative length when we prepend alternating prefixes — sometimes the cum_len calculation doesn't account for packed rows.
maya: FP16 run shows no warnings. INT8 always triggers warning after 7-9k tokens.
ci-bot: job/rjob-2298 queued by dylan (repro run, 4 trials)

(18m later)

dylan: rjob-2298 results: reproduces consistently on quantized path. Root cause narrowed: quant_pack_stride calculation used byte-width (row_bytes) instead of tokens-per-row in rotation routine. When pack compression removes a few trailing zeros, subsequent index calculation shifts by 1 token occasionally.

dylan: PR draft: https://git.redwood/pr/734 (fix: use token stride and add alignment asserts)

maya: Nice find. Any perf impact from using token-stride math instead of byte-stride?

dylan: Microbenchmarks show negligible difference. I added a unit test that runs a randomized long-context pattern to assert kv indices remain monotonic after repeated wraps.

sara: Can we backport to stable-2024-11? Several customers using quant8 on dedicated are impacted.

dylan: Will open backport PR and tag RELEASE_NOTE: kv-cache INT8 alignment fix. Also adding a canary job across dedicated nodes.

maya: Follow-up: I'll kick off a monte-carlo suite of 50 randomized prepend sequences across 10 seeds to be safe.

ci-bot: deploy/canary: canary rollout started on dedicated-dev/kv-fix :rocket:

tomas: Marking as current fix-in-progress. If monte-carlo passes -> close.

maya: Monte-carlo run — first 50/50 green, pushing 200 runs now.

dylan: Backport PR created: https://git.redwood/pr/742 — requesting review from @tomas and @ana

ana: quick review ACK, left one nit on test naming. Good to backport.

maya: Thanks all. Reopen if we see any residual flakiness; otherwise resolved for now. :white_check_mark:
